records.region: Southeast Alaska, Chickamin Glacier and Chickamin River coastal drainage near the British Columbia border
records.geographic_disambiguation: Chickamin River is supported as the representative receiving-system name. One newly acquired and actually read USGS original covers both mainstem fragments, all 36 stored parts, the Chickamin Glacier opening and arc, glacier-margin lake/outlet setting, continuously labeled river valley, South Fork and Leduc receiving joins, lower meanders and separate source/render coastal endings. Geographic correspondence is complete at ordinary terrain scale; the name is not imposed uniformly on glacier, lake, tributary or render-extension components.
records.completion_scope: All 36 stored parts across the two selected mainstem fragments, the glacier-to-lake outlet passage, named river valley and separate source/render coastal endings have ordinary geographic correspondence. Chickamin River is a representative receiving-system identity, with glacier and tributary names kept separate.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity for the researched glacier-to-coast composite through its continuously mapped Chickamin River receiving valley. It does not rename Chickamin Glacier, the unnamed glacier-margin lake, separately named tributaries, or the generalized coastal render extension.

scope_limits: No formal registry lookup was performed; accepted, scalar and Korean names remain null.
The glaciated opening is geographic correspondence, not evidence of present surface/subglacial flow or a precise natural-river source.
The lake name and marine receiving-waterbody name were not established and are not invented.

A generalized selected path may traverse mapped lake margins, braid floors or coastal slopes without matching a present active thread. The source mouth and rendered coastal extension are deliberately described separately.
The original multiscale map has no single established imagery/survey epoch for this reading; no exact bank, tidal-stage, present glacier-front or legal name-boundary claim is made.

records.region: Buenaventura, Valle del Cauca; western Farallones-to-Pacific corridor
records.material_pending_reason: The selected first southern side-valley approaches the clearly visible east–west receiver near the first/second-part transition. The receiver and a separate northern junction are readable, but haze, cloud and canopy obscure the intervening trough and southern side-valley mouth. The ordinary valley connection itself cannot be distinguished confidently from forested slope texture. This is not merely an unseen wet thread, exact bank or first coordinate. Regional prose does not locate this short chosen branch.
records.geographic_disambiguation: A bounded downstream Río Cajambre identification is retained below. It is not promoted to the complete selected composite while its chosen opening through-link is unestablished.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research pass is complete. All48parts are explicitly accounted for;47parts have ordinary correspondence, while the first-part opening requires independent usable terrain evidence. Further source expansion was stopped after one useful overview and one opening detail. This is one source-material-pending state, not a completed name-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: A bounded downstream Río Cajambre identification is retained below. It is not promoted to the complete selected composite while its chosen opening through-link is unestablished.

scope_limits: The only primary material gap is the first southern side-valley’s outlet into the visible east–west receiver near the first/second-part transition. The intervening trough and side-valley mouth remain indistinct at terrain scale through haze/cloud and canopy; local slope texture alone is insufficient to establish that through-link.
The Agua Sucia association is bounded to the southern approach at the major confluence. No exact first feeder name, upstream name-change location or whole-river scalar name is established.
Imagery is a mosaic with unspecified local epochs. No present flow, exact banks, navigation condition or tidal operation is certified.
The two prose sources are distinct projects but may share earlier CVC descriptions. They do not constitute formal naming-registry verification.
The modeled81.451km length is selected-render metadata, not an independently verified natural-river length.

records.region: Lassen County, northeastern California, United States
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative lower receiving river system for this selected tributary, slough and terminal-lake composite. It does not rename the separately named upper creeks, delta sloughs or Honey Lake.
records.completion_scope: The selected eastern feeder joins Bull Creek and Deep Creek, crosses the common receiving floor into mapped Secret Creek, rounds Shaffer Mountain to Willow Creek, and reaches the lower Susan River and its slough/wetland plain before ending inside Honey Lake. Susan River is supported as a representative receiving-system identity only.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative lower receiving river system for this selected tributary, slough and terminal-lake composite. It does not rename the separately named upper creeks, delta sloughs or Honey Lake.

scope_limits: Representative Susan River identity does not mean every selected reach or lake bears that name.

The geographic table lists Deep Creek and Secret Creek as tributary to Snowstorm Creek, then Petes Creek and Willow Creek. National Map labels on the actual selected middle corridor use Secret Creek. These sources are not silently harmonized; the lower Willow–Susan–Honey relationship agrees.
Continuous receiving-floor and slough-plain correspondence does not establish present flow, every operating diversion, a precise channel through each field, or exact name-transition vertices.
The complete target ending is in a lake interior; no ordinary river channel is claimed across that lake.
No current official registry, Indigenous alternate form, Korean name or common source-layer survey date was verified.
